Sleep that runs past midnight counts toward the day you woke up.
Your need settles after 14 nights. Using 7 h 45 min as the baseline until then.
Baseline from your own recent nights.
Needs at least 3 recent nights to learn your usual wake time.
Bedtime is worked back from your usual wake time and how efficiently you sleep.
Sleep performance blends four parts: duration against your need (40 percent), restorative stages (25), efficiency (20) and consistency (15).
Your need is a baseline of 7 h 45 min, or the 75th percentile of your last 30 nights once 14 exist, plus extra for yesterday\'s strain and half of your recent sleep debt, up to 10 h.
Restorative sleep is deep plus REM as a share of time asleep. Efficiency is time asleep over time in bed. Consistency is how closely your bed and wake times match over the last 7 days.
A part that cannot be measured, such as stages on a night scored by movement alone, drops out and the others are scaled up. This is a summary of your sleep, not medical advice.
Needs at least 4 recorded nights in the last week before Apex counts a debt.
100 means the same sleep and wake times every day, 0 is no more regular than chance, and below 0 is the opposite pattern. Calculated over the last week.
Needs at least two comparable days of sleep in the last week.

How far your heart rate falls asleep compared with the day. A fall of 10 percent or more is called a dipper. A smaller dip can follow late exercise, alcohol, heat, illness or a short night. It is context, not a diagnosis.
No daytime heart rate to compare with.
Too few minutes of heart rate, day or night, to compare.
The heart-rate dip could not be worked out for this night.
